_doc: Every instrument that decides whether an output is correct: a grader, scorer, equivalence check, or data loader. Each has a positive_test (proves it accepts a known-correct input) and a negative_test (proves it rejects a known-wrong one). Test commands use sys.executable (the venv interpreter at .venv/bin/python); any subprocess inside a test also uses sys.executable, never bare `python`. A grader that cannot run MUST raise, never return a false verdict. Run a single node: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest <node> -q`. If nothing here judges an output it is listed under not_applicable with a reason.

instruments.name: mnist_data_loader
instruments.what_it_decides: What dataset every arm runs on. Fingerprints the paper's own MNIST by (a) raw IDX file sha256, (b) label vocabulary {0..9} + the canonical per-class histogram, (c) size/shape (60000 train / 10000 test, 784-dim, float32 in [0,1]) and the 50000/10000 split. A synthetic or corrupted corpus is REJECTED, so a closed-book fallback to chance-level numbers cannot pass undetected.
instruments.requires_tools: external: MNIST raw IDX files under mnist/ (downloaded by fgsm_repro.data from cvdf-datasets / ossci S3 mirrors). If absent the loader raises, not silently substitutes.

instruments.name: eval_clean
instruments.what_it_decides: Clean classification accuracy = mean(argmax(logits)==y) (binary: sign(score)). Decides whether a model's clean prediction is correct. Empty input raises (test_eval_clean_raises_on_empty), never returns a vacuous 0.0.

instruments.name: eval_fgsm_error_and_confidence
instruments.what_it_decides: Adversarial error_rate (fraction of ALL examples misclassified on the model's own FGSM examples) and mean_confidence_on_errors (softmax prob of the predicted class, averaged over the MISCLASSIFIED subset only; 0.0 when none wrong). This is the metric behind every FGSM-error claim (M1/M2/M3/M6/M7).

instruments.name: eval_fgsm_attack
instruments.what_it_decides: The FGSM attack+eval end-to-end: at eps=0 it equals the clean error (limiting case), at eps>0 it increases error (the paper's central phenomenon). Guards against an attack that ignores the perturbation.

instruments.name: eval_transfer
instruments.what_it_decides: Cross-model transfer: craft FGSM on a source model, score on a target. Self-transfer equals own FGSM (positive); an independent target gives a valid, separately-computed metric (negative proves the target is actually used). Backs the M6 transfer claims.

instruments.name: class_agreement
instruments.what_it_decides: Cross-model class agreement (tex:679-688): over m1's FGSM-error subset, how often m2 picks m1's (wrong) class; and over the both-wrong subset. Identical models agree perfectly (positive); an independent model does not (negative). Backs the M8 agreement claims.

instruments.name: rbf_confidence_grader
instruments.what_it_decides: RBF UNNORMALIZED per-class confidence exp(q_k) (SPEC §6 item 9): high at a class centre, decaying toward 0 off-manifold. This is the only reading that can reproduce the paper's 1.2% conf-on-mistakes / 60.6% clean-confidence / 0% rubbish-error (a softmax reading is bounded below by 1/K and cannot). Backs the M8/M9 RBF claims.

instruments.name: rubbish_sampler_and_fooling_step
instruments.what_it_decides: Rubbish-example instrument (appendix, tex:905-954): sample_rubbish draws x~N(0,I_dim); fooling_sign_step takes a gradient-sign step raising a target class's probability. Standard-normal (positive, known mean 0 / var 1) vs non-constant (negative). Backs the M9 rubbish claims.

instruments.name: e6_closed_form_oracle
instruments.what_it_decides: The closed-form worst-case adversarial logistic loss E6 = E zeta(y(eps*||w||_1 - w^T x - b)) (tex:410-412). Used as a constructed-truth oracle: it equals the empirical FGSM loss for y=+1 (positive, same-quantity-two-ways) and is >= the clean loss (negative, worst-case not best-case).

instruments.name: degeneracy_equivalence_check
instruments.what_it_decides: Equivalence: the FGSM adversarial-training method (E7) at its no-op eps=0 reproduces the baseline (clean training) EXACTLY at the cost level, the training-state level, and the CLI level. The cheapest real correctness evidence; a wrong implementation diverges here in seconds. The negative arm (dropout ON) shows the check is meaningful — with dropout the two DO diverge, so the no-op equality is not a tautology.

instruments.name: fgsm_perturbation_invariants
instruments.what_it_decides: Structural invariants of the FGSM attack itself: ||eta||_inf == eps, no clipping, eps=0 identity, sign(0)=0 convention. These are equivalence checks on the attack's own output, independent of any trained model.

instruments.name: numbers_gate_scalar_evaluator
instruments.what_it_decides: Whether a scalar claim (ordering/value/existence/invariant) holds: resolves measured.<arm>.<metric> tokens from measured.json at every seed and evaluates the claim arithmetic; missing data BLOCKS, never fabricates.
instruments.positive_test: tests/test_measured_resolver.py::test_single_element_list_pointer_collapses_to_scalar (plus the gate's own clean run over the 34 scalar claims: claims_result.json 31 pass / 3 annotated low fails)

instruments.name: numbers_gate_curve_evaluator
instruments.what_it_decides: Whether a figure 'curve' claim holds (a curve rises, crosses, stays above/below, matches): resolves quantity/against/x SEQUENCES from the arm's per-seed result files (results/_per_seed/), restricts to the figure-read x_range, evaluates the comparison at every seed, and BLOCKS on missing/non-sequence data. Backs the Figure-4 claims fc1..fc3.

instruments.name: claims_quote_verifier
instruments.what_it_decides: Whether every claim's quote is a VERBATIM substring of paper/source/iclr2015.tex starting at the line its citation names; whether claim kinds carry their required arithmetic fields; whether compute-invariance counts are truthful; whether every arm metric pointer resolves in the shipped results.
instruments.positive_test: tests/test_claims_integrity.py::test_every_claim_quote_is_verbatim_at_cited_line (and the field/kind/pointer tests in the same module)
instruments.negative_test: tests/test_claims_integrity.py (a non-verbatim quote, a stale count, a shifted citation line, or an unresolvable pointer each fail loudly)

not_applicable.name: mp_dbm_generative_inference
not_applicable.reason: The paper's generative-resistance test (tex:827-833, MP-DBM 97.5% on FGSM) is in claims.json not_tested: we do not implement MP-DBM inference, so no instrument here judges a generative model's adversarial robustness. Settled as BLOCKED/not-tested, not by a grader.

not_applicable.name: cifar10_loader
not_applicable.reason: CIFAR-10 arms (tex:341 conv-maxout 87.15%, tex:911-912 rubbish) are excluded by the scope fixed in SPEC §1; no CIFAR-10 grader or loader is implemented. Claims are in not_tested.
